title: Lesson 1 Quiz: Identify an Economic Problem
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A school district has $54,000 left in this year's budget. It can build handwashing stations at its schools for $54,000, or pay for extra school-bus trips for students in remote villages at $18 per trip. If it builds the handwashing stations, what is the opportunity cost measured in bus trips? (Enter a number only.)
A student is drafting the first sentence of a capstone project. Which version uses the SDG framework most precisely?

choices.text: My problem is about SDG 6, clean water and sanitation, which matters a great deal to families in my town.
My problem touches each of the 17 SDGs at once, since water affects health, school, and work.
My problem affects SDG target 6.1, measured by the share of people using safely managed drinking water.
My problem is a global crisis, so it fits under whichever SDG gets the most public attention this year.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: In a river town, fish catches have fallen for years while factories upstream have expanded and release more waste into the river. Which of these describes an underlying economic cause rather than a symptom?

choices.text: Factories pay nothing for the waste they release, so their private cost is below the social cost.
Fishing families earn less income each year, and some of them have moved away from the town.
Local fish prices have gone up, because fewer fish now reach the town's market each week.
The river looks darker and smells worse than it did ten years ago, especially in summer.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Farmers in a valley pump groundwater for free, and the water table is falling, which will raise pumping costs for everyone in the future. Which explanation of the farmers' behavior uses incentives correctly?

choices.text: Farmers pump a lot because they do not realize that the valley's groundwater is a scarce resource.
Farmers pump a lot because the government has set the price of groundwater too high for them.
Farmers would cut their pumping as soon as future generations asked them to save some of the water.
Each farmer gets the full gain from extra pumping but bears a small share of the falling water table.

questions.prompt: Which is the most researchable problem statement for a capstone project?

choices.text: Our town should introduce a water tax so that its rural schools can install new pumps by next year.
In two rural schools in District K, attendance falls in the dry season; we think unrepaired pumps cause it.
Water is a basic human right, and many millions of people around the world still lack safe access to it today.
Education in our country seems to get worse each year, probably because the government is not doing enough.
